version.changelog: Declare capabilities and require explicit archive confirmation.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a real Notion sync tool, but it asks for broader environment and web access than its scripts need and includes an explicit local path-safety override.

dimensions.detail: The manifest allows Env and WebFetch even though the bundled scripts read only NOTION_API_KEY through process.env and make fixed HTTPS requests to api.notion.com. This is broader agent authority than the implementation appears to require if the host does not strictly scope secrets and outbound network use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package installer, dependency install, or auto-run hook was found. Setup does ask users to configure a Notion integration token and, for OpenClaw protected mode, persistent gateway secret-egress settings.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most high-impact actions are user-directed: batch query updates require a filter, archiving requires --confirm-archive, and local file access is workspace-restricted by default. The documented --allow-unsafe-paths override can intentionally bypass that boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, service, startup hook, or automatic persistence was found. The watch command writes a disclosed state file, and the documentation gives an optional cron example that would require separate user setup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Notion search, export, create, update, batch-update, inspect, monitor, and archive capabilities are disclosed and match the stated Notion sync purpose; no hidden unrelated payload was found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. Use a Notion integration token scoped only to the pages and databases you intend to expose, prefer protected secrets bound to api.notion.com, and avoid granting broad Env/WebFetch access if your host can narrow the tool allowlist. Use --dry-run and filters for batch updates, and use --allow-unsafe-paths only for an exact path you intentionally want the agent to read from or write to.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The --allow-unsafe-paths flag is present and disables the default workspace boundary for user-selected file paths. It is clearly documented and not automatic, but users should treat it as a privileged override.
[T05] unexpected: The overbroad Env and WebFetch allowlist concern is supported by the artifact: those tools are granted in SKILL.md, while the scripts use process.env only for NOTION_API_KEY and route API traffic through api.notion.com.
